Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8.note: ★ HARNESS PORT DONE AND MEASURED; the residual is a THRESHOLD question, not a defect. Four real harness defects were found and fixed (2fcea05b): the warm cargo target dir was never warmed and pointed at the wrong path, so the agent's first `cargo test` cold-built the dep tree and hit the 180 s command timeout; `run_shell` read both pipes to EOF before child.wait(), so any `cargo run &` -- which the prompt invites -- burned the full timeout and returned nothing; `ping()` used a line reader, scoring a live newline-less `pong` as dead; and five followed_directions regexes diverged from followed_directions.py. MEASURED before -> after, same box, N=10 tiers: webserver_ok 3/9/6/7 -> 10 and 8; followed_directions 0/6/4/7 -> 9 and 5; Sigma-wall 394-637 s -> 923 and 734 s, with the agent now taking 10-18 turns per run instead of 3-7. One tier reached the full 10/10. REMAINING: 10/10 AND 10/10 is not reachable ON DEMAND. temperature is now 0.3 -- the value the shell harness pins and the one that scored 10/10 there -- so this gate is stochastic by construction. An exact 10-of-10 bar on a stochastic instrument fails a healthy build roughly half the time. OWNER DECISION, deliberately not taken here: either state these bounds as a distribution over k tiers (e.g. best-of-2, or a mean with a floor), or keep the exact bar and accept re-runs. Lowering the counts to today's draw is still the wrong move, which is why they are unchanged. The ENGINE is not in question: the shell harness scored webserver_ok 10/10 and cargo_valid 10/10 on this same binary. || original: Gate A (benchmark-pr skill): N=10 agentic-webserver on the 35B MoE flagship — 10/10 webserver_ok, 10/10 followed_directions, Σwall <= 1300 s. The two 10/10 counts are ABSOLUTE correctness bounds and take no noise. ★ Σwall is DELIBERATELY NOT RATCHETED to the 978.13 s best (PR #388, dgx3): unlike the BFCL scores, tier Σwall carries +/-200-300 s of run-to-run noise from single 230-320 s outlier iterations, so a ~978 s ceiling would fail constantly on healthy builds. 1300 s is a BLOWUP DETECTOR, not a perf gate — it cannot see a 5-10% TTFT regression, which is what the two TTFT gates are for. Historical band Σwall 950-1287 s; high-water (fastest) 978.13 s recorded here for reference only. Walls are box-specific: compare like-for-like or not at all. || ★ `iterations` is PINNED at exactly 10, the N the two 10/10 bounds are written for. A count bound alone does not describe the run that produced it: `webserver_ok >= 10` is satisfied by 12 successes out of 20, and Σwall <= 1300 s is satisfied by 5 iterations. Neither is the gate. This adds a threshold, it does not relax one -- the recorded runs all carry iterations 10.
